subject: Stair-step rollback & seasonal carve-out redlines for pricing schedule
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@clearsky.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearsky.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing schedule redline — request for seasonal carve-out + rollback language

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. We reviewed the Exhibit A pricing schedule and uploaded a redline with a couple of asks that are material for our finance team: a seasonal carve-out for our Q4 promotional months, and a stair-step rollback clause for sustained volume declines beyond an annual true-up.

Key asks in the attached redline (Exhibit-Pricing_v3_redline.docx):
- Seasonal carve-out: exclude promotional months Nov–Dec from the minimum committed usage calculation (we propose carving out 8 weeks).
- Stair-step rollback: if actual monthly usage falls below 65% of committed run-rate for two consecutive quarters, ClearSky can request a rollback of the committed tier to the nearest lower step with a 30-day notice; the rollback must not retroactively adjust prior invoices.

We understand Redwood's need for revenue predictability — the team added a proposed guardrail (a one-time stabilization fee or a short-term surcharge) in the redline, and we want to confirm if Redwood will accept the rollback trigger and the non-retroactivity language.

Also looped in procurement for contracting cadence. We attached the redline and a spreadsheet showing expected seasonal variances. Can you review and confirm which items are deal-breakers versus items Redwood can accept with concessions?

Regards,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Director, Strategic Sourcing | ClearSky Health

Attachments: Exhibit-Pricing_v3_redline.docx, ClearSky_CTR_schedule.xlsx

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@clearsky.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule redline — request for seasonal carve-out + rollback language

Jordan — thanks for sending. I reviewed the redline and the spreadsheet. High level: we are open to a limited seasonal carve-out and to a rollback mechanism but need to tighten the triggers and compensation approach to protect committed capacity planning.

Looping in Aditya (account lead) and Laura (legal) to weigh in on the commercial and contract language. Two quick clarifying asks from our side so we can make an internal recommendation:
1) For the seasonal carve-out, confirm whether ClearSky expects zero recognition of those weeks toward the minimum or a reduced weighting (e.g., 25% credit).
2) For the rollback: does ClearSky require an immediate billing tier adjustment upon 30-day notice, or would you accept a deferred adjustment after the next quarterly true-up?

I can put together a proposed middle-ground: allow a single seasonal carve-out window per contract year (8 weeks) with a 25% credit applied to committed minimums for that window; and allow a rollback only after two consecutive quarters below threshold, effective at the next quarterly true-up, plus a one-time stabilization fee (pro-rated) to cover short-term reallocation costs.

If that sounds reasonable I'll draft specific redline language for Exhibit A and ask Laura to propose clean contract wording.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: ClearSky redline — commercial view

Folks — quick internal notes before Laura drafts legal language.

Commercial stance: we should aim to accept the concept but narrow the scope. Specific recommendations:
- Seasonal carve-out: accept a single carve-out window up to 6 weeks (not 8) per contract year, and apply a 50% credit (so usage during the window counts as 50% toward minimums). That reduces revenue volatility for Redwood while giving ClearSky some relief.
- Rollback trigger: change threshold to <60% of committed run-rate for two consecutive quarters, and make the rollback effective at the subsequent quarterly true-up (no retroactivity).
- Stabilization fee: instead of a one-time surcharge, suggest a capped rebalancing fee equal to 10% of one month of committed TCV, payable once on the rollback effective date.

Operational considerations:
- We need to ensure billing systems can accept partial credits and apply them only to minimum calculations (not to per-token rates).
- Product (Karthik) — confirm whether model capacity guarantees could be affected if we lower committed tiers mid-contract.

If product/legal sign off I think this is a fair compromise.

-Aditya

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@clearsky.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule redline — legal redlines and requested edits

Jordan — thanks for the redline. I've attached a concise markup of Exhibit A with two sets of edits: (1) we accept a seasonal carve-out but with reduced credit and clearer timing; (2) we will accept a rollback mechanism with tightened triggers, effective at the next quarterly true-up and subject to a capped stabilization fee. See summary below and the attached Exhibit-Pricing_v3_redline.docx for line edits.

Legal summary of changes we propose:
- Seasonal carve-out: "Customer may designate, once per Contract Year, up to six (6) consecutive weeks as a Seasonal Carve-Out. Usage during the Seasonal Carve-Out will be credited at fifty percent (50%) toward the Minimum Committed Usage for such Contract Year."
- Rollback: "If Customer's actual usage is less than sixty percent (60%) of the then-applicable committed run-rate for two (2) consecutive Contract Quarterly periods, Customer may request a reduction to the next lower committed tier. Any such reduction will be effective at the first day of the quarterly true-up following written notice and will not apply retroactively to prior invoices. Customer will pay a one-time rebalancing fee equal to ten percent (10%) of one month's committed fees upon the effective date of the tier reduction."
- We added a provision requiring reasonable evidence of the usage decline (billing reports) and a 30-day review period before a reduction is finalized.

Please confirm if ClearSky can accept the 50% credit and the 6-week cap; if not, specify preferred alternative language and we'll aim to compromise. Also open to a short phone call to walk through the calculation example in your spreadsheet.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Exhibit-Pricing_v3_redline.docx

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@clearsky.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearsky.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule redline — acceptance of framework, minor asks

Laura/Stephanie — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear language. The framework you proposed is acceptable in principle. Two small follow-ups before we finalize:
1) ClearSky requests that the rebalancing fee cap be expressed in USD rather than as a percentage for predictability (we propose a cap of $25,000 for the rebalancing fee).
2) For the evidence requirement, procurement asks that Redwood agree to deliver a standard CSV extract of the usage ledger for the two quarters under review within 10 business days of receiving a notice. We can sign off if those two items are added to the Exhibit.

If Redwood agrees, we can proceed with your edited Exhibit and then circulate for signature via DocuSign. I included a DocuSign request link below for the contract once redlines are finalized.

DocuSign request: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC123-example

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Director, Strategic Sourcing | ClearSky Health

Attachments referenced: stair-rollback-illustration.pdf
